title: O2 volume-time curves and initial rate vs concentration (order from graph)
summary: Top graph: volume of O2 (cm3) against time (s) for five initial concentrations of H2O2(aq) (0.40, 0.32, 0.24, 0.16, 0.080 mol dm^-3), with tangents drawn at t = 0 for the first curves. Bottom graph: the initial rate of formation of oxygen (cm3 s^-1) against initial concentration is a straight line through the origin, so the initial rate is directly proportional to [H2O2(aq)] and the reaction is first order with respect to H2O2(aq).

blocks.text: Volume of O2 (cm3) vs Time (s). Five curves labelled 1-5 with [H2O2(aq)] = 0.40, 0.32, 0.24, 0.16, 0.080 mol dm^-3. Y axis 0 to 28 (ticks every 2), X axis 0 to 180 (ticks every 20). All curves start at origin, rise steeply then level off.
(blue) 'tangent' with two blue tangent lines drawn from the origin on curves 1 and 2; circled numbers 1-5 beside curves

Initial rate of formation of oxygen (cm3 s^-1) vs Initial concentration of hydrogen peroxide solution (mol dm^-3). Y axis 0 to 0.5 (ticks 0.1), X axis 0 to 0.5 (ticks 0.1). Five points (labelled 1-5) lie on a straight line through the origin.
Right: 'rate' (y axis) and '[A]' (x axis) sketch; 'proportional symbol: directly proportional'. Left: 'Common in DSE'; 'Deduce the order of reaction from graph'
'Graph is a straight line. / Slope = 1 / Initial rate proportional to [H2O2(aq)] therefore order of reaction with respect to H2O2(aq) is 1.'

volume_time_graph.note: Plateau values are read by eye from the graph (approximate, +/- 0.5 cm3). Individual curve points are not tabulated on the page. Plateau is roughly proportional to concentration (about 66 cm3 per mol dm^-3). Curves appear to reach about 80-90% of their plateau by t = 60-80 s.

x_axis.label: Initial concentration of hydrogen peroxide solution (mol dm^-3)

y_axis.label: Initial rate of formation of oxygen (cm3 s^-1)
y_axis.note: top tick 0.5, axis arrow extends slightly above

rate_concentration_graph.line: straight line through the origin, passing close to all five points; gradient about 1.2-1.3 cm3 s^-1 per mol dm^-3 (read by eye)
rate_concentration_graph.note: Point values are read by eye (approximate); the page prints no numeric table.

data.handwritten_conclusion: Graph is a straight line; 'Slope = 1' (student's note); initial rate proportional to [H2O2(aq)]; order of reaction with respect to H2O2(aq) is 1

key_concepts: Higher initial [H2O2] gives a steeper curve at t = 0 (larger initial rate) and a larger final O2 volume
Initial rate = gradient of tangent at t = 0 on each volume-time curve
Rate vs concentration straight line through the origin means rate is directly proportional to concentration
Therefore first order with respect to H2O2(aq): rate = k[H2O2]
Deducing order from a graph is common in DSE

animation.concept: Each curve's tangent at t = 0 gives one point on the rate-concentration graph; five points form a straight line through the origin, so rate is proportional to [H2O2] and the order is 1.
animation.why: This is the table-to-graph mapping step of the method: five tangent slopes become five points on a second graph. Showing the gradients migrating from graph 1 to graph 2 explains how the two graphs on the page are connected.

steps.visual: Left panel: axes x 'Time (s)' 0-180 (ticks 20), y 'Volume of O2 (cm3)' 0-28 (ticks 2). Five curves draw in sequence as saturating exponentials V = Vmax(1 - e^(-t/tau)) with Vmax about 26.5, 21, 16, 10.8, 5.7 (concentration 0.40, 0.32, 0.24, 0.16, 0.080), colours dark to light, each tagged with a circled number 1-5 and '[H2O2(aq)] = ...mol dm^-3' at the right end. Right panel (empty) holds axes x 'Initial concentration (mol dm^-3)' 0-0.5, y 'Initial rate (cm3 s^-1)' 0-0.5.
steps.caption: O2 volume vs time for 5 concentrations of H2O2(aq)

steps.visual: Curve 1 highlighted, others dimmed. A blue tangent line grows from the origin along curve 1's initial slope (about 0.51 cm3 s^-1) up to the top of the plot; label 'tangent'. A dx/dy triangle shows the slope calculation with text 'initial rate = 0.51 cm3 s^-1 (approx.)'.
steps.caption: Tangent at t = 0 gives the initial rate

steps.visual: The slope value flies (small sphere moves along an arc) from the tangent into the right panel and lands as point 1 at (0.40, ~0.51), circled '1'.
steps.caption: One experiment gives one point

steps.visual: Repeat quickly for curves 2 to 5 (0.32 -> ~0.41, 0.24 -> ~0.32, 0.16 -> ~0.215, 0.080 -> ~0.10): each tangent flashes blue, slope flies across, points 2-5 appear with circled numbers. Tangents get visibly shallower.
steps.caption: Repeat for each initial concentration

steps.visual: Best-fit straight line grows from the origin through the five points. Origin ring highlighted. Text: 'straight line through origin'.
steps.caption: Graph is a straight line through the origin

steps.visual: Doubling demonstration: two arrows, x doubles from 0.16 to 0.32 and y roughly doubles (0.215 to ~0.41). Final text: 'Initial rate proportional to [H2O2(aq)] => first order'.
steps.caption: Rate proportional to [H2O2(aq)]: first order

elements: two flat panels with gridlines, axes, tick labels and arrowheads
5 curve polylines with distinct colours and circled number sprites
blue tangent line segment, dx/dy right-triangle lines
5 point spheres on right panel with number sprites
text sprites for axis labels, slope readouts, concentration tags
correctness_notes: Axis ranges: top graph x 0-180 s, y 0-28 cm3; bottom graph x 0-0.5 mol dm^-3, y 0-0.5 cm3 s^-1
Curve numeric values are approximate readings; do not label them as exact textbook data
Every curve starts at the origin (0,0), rises steeply then flattens to a plateau and never decreases
Initial rate is the gradient at t = 0, not the average gradient over the whole run
Initial rate vs concentration: straight line through the origin means rate proportional to concentration = first order with respect to H2O2(aq)
Y-axis unit of initial rate is cm3 s^-1 (volume of O2 per second), not mol dm^-3 s^-1

The student's note 'Slope = 1' refers to a constant, straight gradient (first order); the plotted line's numeric gradient reads about 1.2-1.3 cm3 s^-1 per mol dm^-3, so do not print 'slope = 1' as a value
